name: nsh v0.4.0
body:
Native Shell 0.4.0 fills out the unstyled component foundation with form controls, rich text and more chart marks; adds shader effects and transitions; runs web apps on the browser's own JavaScript engine; and gives the APIs apps use one consistent shape.

**Upgrading from 0.3.x?** This release includes breaking API changes. See the migration notes below before rebuilding your app.

## Highlights

- **Shaders across the UI.** Draw a view's box with WGSL using `Shader`, draw views and the whole screen through a program with `ShaderEffect`, `ShaderTransition`, `ScreenEffect` and `ScreenTransition`, and let pages and dialogs come and go through one with `transitionShader`. All of it draws on macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, Linux and the web; the GPUI backend draws `Shader` fills. ([#517](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/517), [#682](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/682), [#763](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/763), [#764](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/764), [#765](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/765), [#766](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/766), [#767](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/767), [#768](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/768), [#769](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/769), [#770](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/770))
- **A full set of form controls.** Build forms and toolbars with `Select`, `Combobox`, `Slider`, `NumberInput`, `OtpInput`, `DatePicker`, `Calendar`, `TimeField`, `ColorPicker`, `Toggle` / `ToggleGroup`, `Toolbar`, `Link`, `Pagination`, `Avatar` / `AvatarGroup` and `Accordion`. They provide behavior, state and accessibility; your app supplies their look. ([#536](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/536), [#585](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/585), [#510](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/510), [#534](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/534), [#535](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/535), [#598](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/598), [#577](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/577), [#621](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/621), [#702](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/702), [#624](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/624), [#690](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/690), [#706](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/706), [#610](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/610))
- **Rich content and navigation.** Edit documents with `RichEditor`, a ProseMirror-style editor with tables; add a command palette with `Command`, nested lists with `Tree`, slides with `Carousel`, hover previews with `HoverCard` and scroll bars in your own look with `Scrollbar`. `TextView` typesets formulas out of the box. ([#494](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/494), [#518](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/518), [#785](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/785), [#725](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/725), [#722](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/722), [#697](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/697), [#579](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/579), [#841](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/841))
- **More charts from `nsh/base/plot`.** Compose `Bar`, `Pie`, `Arc`, `Sankey`, `Treemap`, `Dot`, `Cell`, `Rule`, `RadialLine` and `RadialGrid` marks with `PlotAxis` and `PlotLabel`, color marks by category, plot against a second y scale, and move a plot's hover with the keyboard and screen readers. ([#505](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/505), [#501](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/501), [#601](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/601), [#867](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/867), [#829](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/829), [#861](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/861), [#819](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/819), [#596](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/596), [#549](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/549), [#599](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/599), [#592](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/592), [#839](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/839), [#521](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/521))
- **Web apps on the browser's own engine.** Every web app now runs on the browser's JavaScript engine, in development with hot updates too. The runtime loads its parts on demand, which takes the gallery's first load from 13.03 MB to 4.35 MB (4.01 MB to 1.41 MB gzipped), and published sites carry Brotli and gzip copies of their files. ([#541](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/541), [#603](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/603), [#853](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/853))
- **More of the system and the toolchain.** Follow whether the app is in use with `lifecycle()`, recognize speech with `Speech.start` on macOS and iOS, read shipped files with `fetch` on `asset:/` URLs, and use WOFF and WOFF2 fonts with fallback along `fontFamily` lists. Rust apps gain file dialogs, system paths, window and menu APIs and `svg()`; an app's crate can register native components in its generated hosts; and `nsh publish <package>` signs an existing package again with another release key. ([#747](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/747), [0520080](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/commit/0520080db), [#746](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/746), [#745](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/745), [#773](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/773), [#629](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/629), [#674](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/674), [#683](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/683), [#886](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/886))

## Performance and platform improvements

- Layout rounds to device pixels, frames that stay on their pixels stay unsent, and a subtree that moves by whole pixels skips its frame walk. Animation graphs evaluate each node once a frame and find interpolation segments by bisection. ([#557](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/557), [#617](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/617), [#637](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/637), [#588](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/588), [#589](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/589), [#590](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/590))
- Images load through one bounded pipeline on the desktops, taking peak memory from about 1.3 GB to about 370 MB when scrolling 1,000 remote photos as thumbnails on Linux. Pasting 474 KB of unbroken text into a multiline `Input` takes 58 ms where it took 12 s on macOS, and `DataTable`, `Editor`, `Select`, `Calendar` and the input controls do less work as they scroll and take keys. ([#674](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/674), [#627](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/627), [#622](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/622), [#604](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/604), [#638](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/638), [#656](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/656), [#817](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/817), [#672](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/672))
- iOS keeps focused inputs above the keyboard and launches on iOS 15 to 17, adds leading and SF Symbol bar buttons, draws backdrop blur behind a view's background, and draws system alerts and the `TabBar` in the app's theme colors. ([#821](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/821), [#888](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/888), [#809](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/809), [#866](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/866), [#742](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/742), [#741](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/741))
- Android fixes `wss://` WebSockets, follows display density changes while the app runs, keeps its runtime classes in minified embedding apps, strips release libraries, and improves keyboard and input handling. ([#530](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/530), [#431](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/431), [#639](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/639), [#538](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/538), [#714](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/714), [#715](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/715), [#717](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/717), [#836](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/836))
- macOS draws fades without redrawing their views, taking one app's memory footprint from 92 MB to 27 MB, and adds trusted web view input with `sendInput` and web view downloads. Linux draws images at device pixels on fractional scales, Windows speeds up plots and gives the wheel to native components, and GPUI delivers files dragged in from other applications and adds see-through windows. ([#877](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/877), [#895](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/895), [#743](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/743), [#758](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/758), [#834](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/834), [#879](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/879), [#712](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/712), [#591](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/591), [#876](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/876))
- The web applies state styles, platform props and scroll views' `contentStyle` and `contentClass`, and passes every event payload field to the app. Selections stay intact across virtual list rows on every platform, arrow keys follow right-to-left layouts, and parts style with `aria-expanded:` and `data-*` attributes. `nsh test` compares values as Jest does. ([#865](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/865), [#885](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/885), [#883](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/883), [#892](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/892), [#703](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/703), [#797](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/797), [#556](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/556), [#815](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/815), [#711](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/711))

## Migrating from 0.3.x

0.4.0 gives each kind of API one shape: styles in CSS's properties, one unit per quantity, one object per event, objects as return values, `on(event, listener)` for listeners, and one way to report failures. The old forms are removed. ([#495](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/495), [#524](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/524), [#533](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/533), [#558](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/558), [#593](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/593), [#612](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/612), [#651](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/651))

Move styling props into `style` and use CSS's shadows. Classes reach all of them too:

```diff
- <View style={{ shadowColor: "#000", shadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 2 }, shadowOpacity: 0.2, shadowRadius: 4 }} />
+ <View style={{ boxShadow: "0 2px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)" }} />
- <Text style={{ textShadowColor: "#000", textShadowOffset: { width: 0, height: 1 }, textShadowRadius: 2 }}>…</Text>
+ <Text style={{ textShadow: "0 1px 2px #000" }}>…</Text>
- <Text numberOfLines={2} ellipsizeMode="middle" selectable>…</Text>
+ <Text style={{ numberOfLines: 2, textOverflow: "ellipsis-middle", userSelect: "text" }}>…</Text>
- <View pointerEvents="box-none" />
+ <View style={{ pointerEvents: "box-none" }} />
- <Image resizeMode="contain" />
+ <Image style={{ objectFit: "contain" }} />
```

Every event handler takes one object, and mouse events carry the DOM's names:

```diff
- <Checkbox onChange={(checked) => …} />
+ <Checkbox onChange={({ checked }) => …} />
- <Input onChange={(text) => …} />
+ <Input onChange={({ value }) => …} />
- <Popover onOpenChange={(open, reason) => …} />
+ <Popover onOpenChange={({ open, reason }) => …} />
- onLayout={(bounds) => bounds.size.width}
+ onLayout={({ bounds }) => bounds.size.width}
- onScrollEnd={(offset) => …}                 // and the drag and momentum events
+ onScrollEnd={({ offset }) => …}
- onLoad={(size) => …}                        // Image
+ onLoad={({ size }) => …}
- onContentSizeChange={(size) => …}
+ onContentSizeChange={({ size }) => …}
- e.translationX, e.translationY, e.velocityX, e.velocityY, e.valueX, e.valueY    // PanEvent
+ e.translation.x, e.translation.y, e.velocity.x, e.velocity.y, e.value?.x, e.value?.y
- keymap.bind("mod+k", (keystroke) => …)
+ keymap.bind("mod+k", ({ keystroke }) => …)
- onHoverIn={…} onHoverOut={…} onHoverMove={(e: HoverEvent) => …}
+ onMouseEnter={…} onMouseLeave={…} onMouseMove={(e: MouseEvent) => …}
```

Functions return objects, options come as one object, and each element has a ref type of its own (`ViewRef`, `InputRef`, `ScrollRef`, `ListRef`, `WebViewRef`, `VideoRef`, `NativeComponentRef`):

```diff
- const finished = await value.timing(1);     // and spring, decay, keyframes, play, start
+ const { finished } = await value.timing(1);
- const last = await value.stop();
+ const { value: last } = await value.stop();
- const id = await AlertDialog.show({ actions: [{ label: "OK" }] });
+ const { action } = await AlertDialog.show({ actions: [{ id: "ok", label: "OK" }] });
- const opened = await openUrl(url);
+ const { opened } = await openUrl(url);
- const count = await editor.replaceAll(text);
+ const { count } = await editor.replaceAll(text);
- if (await Image.prefetch(src)) …
+ await Image.prefetch(src);                  // rejects on failure
- Window.setTitleBar("hidden", 40);
+ Window.setTitleBar({ style: "hidden", height: 40 });
- net.connect(host, port);
+ net.connect({ host, port });
- let node: YNode;
+ let node: ViewRef;
- BackHandler.onBackPress(listener);
+ BackHandler.on("press", listener);
- const sub = host.on(name, listener); sub.remove();
+ const stop = host.on(name, listener); stop();
```

Update these units and names:

```diff
- gestureState.vx                             // points per millisecond, also vy
+ gestureState.vx                             // points per second, also vy
- keyboardFrame().duration                    // seconds
+ keyboardFrame().duration                    // milliseconds
- viewAreaCoveragePercentThreshold: 50, itemVisiblePercentThreshold: 50
+ viewAreaCoverageThreshold: 0.5, itemVisibleThreshold: 0.5
- ImageSize
+ PixelSize
```

Use the `websocket` module's own `connect`, which ends reads cleanly:

```diff
- import { WebSocket } from "websocket"; const c = await WebSocket.connect(url);
+ import { connect } from "websocket"; const c = await connect(url);
- await c.read()                              // rejected on a clean close
+ await c.read()                              // null after a clean close
```

Also update these APIs:

- Handle failures by rejection and `code`: every function returning a promise rejects, a denied capability is an `Error` with `code: "ERR_ACCESS_DENIED"`, `permission` and `resource` (`fetch` keeps a `TypeError` with the same fields), and platforms and quotas report `ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM` and `ERR_NSH_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`. `Clipboard` and `Picker` reject where they are not granted, and `new WebSocket` to a URL not granted fires `error`, then `close` (1006). ([#651](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/651))
- Read `signal` beside `code` in `process.run`'s output; `code` is `null` when a signal ended the child. ([#651](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/651))
- Handle `Clipboard.readImage` rejecting over 48 MB and on Android, and `Clipboard.writeImage` rejecting on Android. ([#701](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/701))
- Add `flexDirection: "column"` to a view that sets `display: "flex"` and stacks its children: that display lays them out in a row, as in CSS. ([#495](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/495))
- Use `start`, `end`, `marginStart`, `paddingEnd` and their relatives for sides that follow the direction: `left`, `right`, `paddingLeft`, `textAlign: "left"` and their relatives keep their side right to left, as in a browser. ([#495](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/495))
- Give `Window` frames the window's top-left corner, y down from the primary screen's top, on every platform (macOS used the bottom-left corner), and drop `anchorTop`. ([#698](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/698))
- Check `platform.desktop` or `platform.idiom === "desktop"` for the desktop idiom: `idiom` is `"desktop"` exactly where `platform.desktop` is true, and `platform.catalyst` is true under Mac Catalyst in every idiom. ([#705](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/705))
- Leave `focusable` unset on views that are not Tab stops: `focusable={true}` makes any view one. ([#503](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/503))
- Expect arrow keys in `Tabs` and `RadioGroup`: only the group's stop is focusable, and `Tab`'s `onPress` and `Radio`'s `onChange` also fire when the keys move the focus. ([#537](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/537))
- Accept `(error, reset)` in every function given as `ErrorBoundary`'s `fallback`: each one is called, whatever parameters it declares. ([#685](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/685))
- Keep `ios={{…}}` and `desktop={{…}}` to their typed keys: an unknown key fails the type check. ([#667](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/667))
- Size elements in a component's slots yourself where they relied on stretching: a slot takes its element's own box, laid out as the component's item. ([#606](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/606))
- Set your theme's `primary` to choose `TabBar`'s selected color, which now follows that token. ([#741](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/741))
- Use `nsh run --port <port>` or `--port 0` to run apps side by side: a plain `nsh run` replaces the NSH session on its port. ([#428](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/428))
- Add `--abi arm64-v8a,armeabi-v7a,x86_64` to `nsh package --target android` when you ship `x86_64`: the default is `arm64-v8a` and `armeabi-v7a`, and `--run` still adds `x86_64` on an x86_64 emulator. ([#539](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/539))
- On the web, call `await player.runModule(entryURL, { appId, capabilities, chunks })` in place of `player.run(bytecode, …)` on custom pages, and import `List`, `Image`, `Canvas`, `WebView` and `Video` from `nsh` in place of their former module paths. App code runs in the page's realm, so browser APIs follow the browser's CORS, permission and secure-context rules. ([#541](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/541), [#603](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/603), [#700](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/700))
- In `nsh/test`, import `PickRequest` in place of `Pick`, allow for `app.clock` being `null`, write `text:` before literal text shaped like a selector prefix, handle `ERR_NSH_TEST_UNSUPPORTED` for `open` options a `--target` cannot honor, expect Jest's `toBe` and `toEqual`, and pass `network: "live"` for real sockets and WebSockets. ([#684](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/684), [#708](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/708), [#710](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/710), [#711](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/711), [#719](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/719))

In Rust, update these as well:

```diff
- text(s).ellipsize_mode(EllipsizeMode::Middle).selectable(true)
+ text(s).text_overflow(EllipsizeMode::Middle).select_text()
- image(src).resize_mode(ResizeMode::Contain)
+ image(src).object_fit(ResizeMode::Contain)
- .on_hover_in(|_: &()| ..) .on_hover_out(|_: &()| ..) .on_hover_move(|e: &HoverEvent| ..)
+ .on_mouse_enter(|e: &MouseEvent| ..) .on_mouse_leave(|e: &MouseEvent| ..) .on_mouse_move(|e: &MouseEvent| ..)
- .action("OK") .cancel("Cancel") .destructive("Delete")
+ .action("ok", "OK") .cancel("cancel", "Cancel") .destructive("delete", "Delete")
- area().y0(0.0)
+ area().y0(AreaY0::from(0.0))
- Scale::Point, Scale::Linear { domain }
+ Scale::Point { reverse: false }, Scale::Linear { domain, reverse: false }
- nsh_core::element::ambient::watch_scroll
+ nsh_core::element::watch_scroll
- nsh-core = "0.3"
+ nsh-core = { version = "0.4", features = ["declarations"] }    # where you read declarations
```

- Take `Size<DevicePixels>` in `image().on_load`, and set `Viewability`'s `view_area_coverage_threshold` and `item_visible_threshold` as `Percentage`. ([#524](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/524))
- Pass `line_height` a `LineHeight`, and handle `Prefetch`'s `Result<(), String>`. ([#495](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/495), [#593](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/593))
- Forward a generic helper's listener to `on_press` as `IntoListener<PressEvent, M>`. ([#629](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/629))
- Read `GridProps`' `x` and `y` as `Prop<Option<Vec<f64>>>`, and end full `Environment` struct literals with `..Default::default()`. ([#839](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/839), [#747](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/747))
- Build `nsh-platform-web` with its `browser` feature, and drop `Bundle::with_harden_bytecode` and `harden_bytecode`. ([#603](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/603))

The compatibility baseline is still being prepared; 0.4.0 is not a frozen compatibility release.

name: nsh v0.3.0
body:
Native Shell 0.3.0 expands the unstyled component foundation with editors, tables, dockable workspaces and charts; improves layout, scrolling and animation; and brings a simpler module structure to Rust and TSX apps.

**Upgrading from 0.2.x?** This release includes breaking API changes. See the migration notes below before rebuilding your app.

## Highlights

- **Editors and data-heavy interfaces.** Build code editing and review tools with `Editor` and `DiffView`, large tables with `DataTable` and `Table`, and dockable workspaces with `DockArea`, `ResizablePanelGroup` and `ResizablePanel`. These components provide behavior and state; your app supplies their look. ([#321](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/321), [#452](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/452), [#458](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/458))
- **More UI building blocks.** Add expandable content with `Collapsible`, task progress with `Progress`, notifications with `Toast` / `ToastStack` / `ToastManager`, and charts with `Plot`, `Line`, `Area` and `Grid` from `nsh/base/plot`. ([#347](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/347), [#352](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/352), [#386](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/386), [#403](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/403))
- **Richer motion and scrolling.** Compose keyframes, motion presets and `createMotion`; use sticky positioning and animated sticky offsets; load more items at the start of a list; and draw custom pull-to-refresh indicators. Desktop and iOS animations now draw at the display’s refresh rate. ([#387](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/387), [#374](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/374), [#376](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/376), [#369](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/369), [#433](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/433), [#436](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/436))
- **Closer integration with embedding apps.** Exchange messages through the host channel, route external URLs through the host, override embedded theme tokens on mobile, and use the system tab bar through `TabBar` from `nsh/mobile`. ([#378](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/378), [#388](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/388), [#377](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/377), [#423](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/423))
- **More resilient screens and images.** Isolate rendering failures with `ErrorBoundary`, pick photos as native files, display `data:` and `blob:` image sources, position images with `objectPosition`, and reuse downloaded images from disk across launches. ([#370](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/370), [#390](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/390), [#375](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/375), [#371](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/371), [#383](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/383))

## Performance and platform improvements

- Layout updates visit only the parts a change can move, unchanged text measurements avoid repeated layout, and lists bind visible rows before pacing their overscan. ([#368](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/368), [#410](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/410), [#328](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/328))
- iOS gains Liquid Glass, selectable system materials for backdrop blur, sharper images on 3× screens, and fixes for swipe-back navigation and keyboard interaction. ([#338](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/338), [#359](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/359), [#362](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/362), [#430](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/430), [#443](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/443))
- Android adds `armeabi-v7a` runtime builds and 16 KB page-size alignment, with fixes for back handling, native component cleanup and text input. ([#420](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/420), [#422](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/422), [#341](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/341), [#340](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/340), [#421](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/421), [#480](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/480))
- Desktop and web fixes improve scrolling, focus, shortcuts, text rendering and accessibility. `nsh check` and `nsh test` now also run Cargo checks and tests for apps with Rust crates. ([#327](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/327), [#302](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/302), [#322](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/322), [#405](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/405), [#434](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/434))

## Migrating from 0.2.x

0.3.0 gives each API one home: primitives, environment and capabilities in `nsh`; unstyled functional components in `nsh/base`; and platform-specific APIs in `nsh/mobile` and `nsh/desktop`. The old import paths are removed. ([#488](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/488))

```diff
- import { Clipboard } from "nsh/clipboard";
+ import { Clipboard } from "nsh";
- import { Input, type InputProps } from "nsh";
+ import { Input, type InputProps } from "nsh/base";
- import { Keyboard, safeAreaInsets } from "nsh/base";
+ import { Keyboard, safeAreaInsets } from "nsh";
- import { BackHandler } from "nsh/android";
- import { InputAccessoryView } from "nsh/ios";
+ import { BackHandler, InputAccessoryView } from "nsh/mobile";
```

The former `nsh/animated`, `nsh/device`, `nsh/gesture`, `nsh/clipboard`, `nsh/host`, `nsh/picker`, `nsh/storage`, `nsh/keymap`, `nsh/native`, `nsh/accessibility`, `nsh/image`, `nsh/list`, `nsh/canvas`, `nsh/webview` and `nsh/video` exports now come from `nsh`.

Use CSS environment values for safe-area and keyboard spacing, and `View selectable` for text selection:

```diff
- <SafeAreaView edges={["top"]}>…</SafeAreaView>
+ <View style={{ paddingTop: "env(safe-area-inset-top)" }}>…</View>
- <KeyboardAvoidingView behavior="padding">…</KeyboardAvoidingView>
+ <View class="pb-[env(keyboard-inset-height)]">…</View>
- <SelectionArea>…</SelectionArea>
+ <View selectable>…</View>
```

Also update these APIs:

- Pass a `Tooltip` element to `tooltip` in place of a string.
- Use `Toast` / `ToastManager` from `nsh/base` in place of Android’s `Toast.show`.
- Use `platform.os` in place of the former iOS / Android `isAvailable` exports.
- In Rust, replace `nsh_core::ui` imports with `nsh_core::element`, use `nsh_core::prelude`, and rename `element::element` to `element::builder`. Use `nsh_base::{nav_stack, nav_page, dialog, alert_dialog}` for navigation and dialogs.

The compatibility baseline is still being prepared; 0.3.0 is not a frozen compatibility release. ([#496](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/pull/496))

## Downloads

Prebuilt toolchains are available below for **macOS Apple Silicon**, **Linux x86_64** and **Windows x86_64**, alongside the **iOS** and **Android** embedding SDKs. Each archive has a `.sha256` checksum file.

[Documentation and live demos](https://nsh.dev) · [Full changelog](https://github.com/longbridge/nsh/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0)
